title: Per-tenant quality fences + adaptive traffic smoothing for embedding model onboarding
creator: Sofia Morales
description:
Problem statement:
We routinely onboard new embedding model variants but lack per-tenant quality gating and adaptive traffic shaping. This leads to (1) noisy global rollouts where a small fraction of tenants experience regressions, (2) inefficient scaling—overloading small serving shards when a tenant spikes, and (3) slow detection of semantic drift in production.

Goal:
Build a production-ready onboarding flow that combines per-tenant quality fences (semantic delta + rerank AUC checks), adaptive traffic smoothing (granular early-stage traffic growth + auto-throttle on latency/quality signals), and a scalable proxy-shard routing mechanism to limit latency impact during soft rollouts.

Success criteria / acceptance:
- Support per-tenant quality fences with thresholds configurable per workspace (default: semantic-similarity delta < 0.06, rerank AUC drop < 0.015).
- Canary traffic grows at controlled cadence (1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 100%) automatically, with automatic rollback when any gating signal crosses thresholds for >5m.
- Proxy-shard routing limits any single tenant's tail latency impact: per-proxy CPU utilization must stay below 70% and P99 latency < 150ms during rollout tests.
- Telemetry dashboards and alerting for semantic drift, cohort quality regressions, and per-tenant rollout state visible in Console by rollout phase.

Design notes / trade-offs:
- Quality fences computed using a lightweight sampling prober that runs offline on a tenant prompt-set. We accept slight probe staleness (up to 24h) to avoid adding per-request cost.
- Adaptive smoothing relies on token-level and request-latency signals from the routing layer. Trade-off: faster ramp gives quicker feedback but higher risk of user-facing regressions. Default cadence errs conservative for enterprise tenants.
- Proxy-shard introduces operational complexity (additional routing tier) but reduces blast radius compared to enlarging global pools. We will start with a single-region pilot to validate.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Prober harness: small service to run quality checks per model/tenant using a tenant-provided or default prompt-set. Exposes results via telemetry. (PR: gh://redwood/embeds/prober/pull/2145)
2) Quality fence API: new metadata on model-catalog entries for default thresholds + per-tenant overrides.
3) Adaptive traffic controller: state machine that increments tenant traffic per configured cadence and listens to telemetry/alerts to throttle or rollback.
4) Proxy-shard routing: change router to shard tenants across proxy workers with token-bucket rate limits; integrates with adaptive controller.
5) Console UX: rollout inspector page with per-tenant view + manual override.
6) Runbook & SLOs: update incident runbook and add new alerts for drift and rollout regressions.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: Deploy prober and quality fence metadata to staging; small-dollar tenants opted-in.
- Week 2: Pilot adaptive controller with 10 tenants (non-critical), monitor for 2 weeks.
- Week 3: Enable proxy-shard routing for pilot tenants; run load tests at 2x expected envelope.
- Week 4: Expand to V1 launch for customers on Dedicated; enterprise gates required for auto-rollout.

Telemetry and gating metrics:
- semantic_delta: median and 95th per-tenant (threshold default 0.06)
- rerank_auc_delta: moving window 30m (threshold default 0.015)
- rollout_p99_latency: compare to tenant baseline (threshold +20% relative)
- proxy_cpu_util, proxy_queue_depth, token_bucket_breaches
- rollout_state: enum {vanguard, canary, gradual, full, rolled_back}
comments: 2025-01-12 - Sofia Morales: Initial scoping doc posted to Confluence: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Embed+Per-Tenant+Quality+Fences (draft). Shared with PM and Design for review.

2025-01-18 - Ravi Patel: Prototype prober implemented. Basic similarity score (cosine) + rerank AUC computation available in gh://redwood/embeds/prober branch 'tenant-prober'. PR created: https://github.com/redwood/embeds-prober/pull/2145

2025-01-22 - Design (Liam O'Connor): UX mockups for Console rollout inspector uploaded: https://drive.redwood.ai/drive/folders/1a2b3-embed-rollout-inspector. Need API to return per-tenant probe history (time-series).

2025-01-28 - QA (Nadia Kim): End-to-end tests for prober + controller added. Found flake: probe worker OOM on large tenant prompt-sets; mitigation: cap sample size and stagger probe runs. See issue ENG-762930.

2025-02-02 - PM (Evan Brooks): Decided to default enterprise tenants to conservative cadence (1%, 3%, 10%, 30%, 100%) and self-serve small tenants to faster cadence. Documented in rollout policy page: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Rollout+Policies

2025-02-04 - Ravi Patel: Pilot deploy to staging (10 tenants) started. Observed two tenants with rerank_auc_delta > 0.02; controller auto-throttled traffic and created rollback tickets. Running detailed analysis with research. Telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/embeds-rollouts/tenant-rollout-overview?orgId=1
